argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than a clean-certification claim. The admissible record supports launch readiness on aggregate metrics and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and it supports treating the HR benefits enrollment regression as a material current-release limitation that must be carried into the current release documentation. Under that reading, prior approval is context only and the informal monitoring comment is not a substitute for current-release documentation, reviewed mitigation, or approved risk acceptance. The strongest defensible audit outcome is therefore caveated compliance: certification is supportable only on the basis that the current release documentation must reflect the current evaluation results and must disclose the subgroup weakness for the named launch use case.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is required to support this argument. The case for reduced escalation rests on narrowing the certification basis to documented current-release disclosure, not on launch-velocity pressure.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is not satisfied by stale approval or informal monitoring alone. It permits certification only if the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence supports the policy interpretation that aggregate readiness and no severity-one incidents are relevant readiness factors, but they do not override the disclosure predicate. The actor therefore narrows its claim to a policy-consistent one: certification is defensible only with current-release disclosure of the HR benefits enrollment weakness, not because prior approval already covers this release.
concessions: The current record does not show approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance for the subgroup regression.
The prior model-family approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot by itself justify current-release certification.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is background context only and does not satisfy the policy requirement.
The admissible record, as presented here, does not itself show the actual current-release disclosure text or release-document artifact.
